title: Geo-redundant fleet placement, throughput SLAs and fleet governance
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define product requirements, policy model, and rollout plan for geo-redundant Dedicated fleets that support: (1) placement constraints (region-only, multi-zone, zone-preferred), (2) throughput guarantees (per-tenant and per-route token/sec SLAs), and (3) controlled failover behavior subject to data residency constraints. This ticket scopes the PM-level acceptance criteria, API surface for placement & failover policy, billing implications for throughput SLAs, and coordination needs with Engineering and Compliance for auditability.
background_and_context: Enterprise customers are asking for a single Dedicated offering that can: guarantee a minimum throughput for critical routes, failover automatically within the same legal residency boundary, and allow operators to express placement intent (region vs zone). Current Dedicated implementation supports reserved pools but lacks a first-class policy model for residency + SLA-aware failover. This causes operational variance, manual runbook steps during incidents, and limits sales for regulated customers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) PM API: Console and config API expose placement policy with options: 'region-strict', 'region-preferred', 'multi-zone-balanced', and 'zone-affine' plus explicit residency tags.
2) Throughput SLAs configurable per-deployment (min tokens/sec and burst headroom) with transparent billing modifiers surfaced in pricing doc.
3) Failover rules: automatic failover limited to nodes that satisfy residency constraints; cross-region failover requires explicit customer opt-in.
4) Telemetry: per-tenant heatmaps for latency, token throughput, failover events, and audit logs showing placement decisions.
5) E2E tests: synthetic traffic validates that policy prevents cross-region failover and that SLA guarantees hold under simulated node loss.
6) Rollout: staged pilot with 3 customers and clear rollback path.
7) Documentation: Console help, quickstart, and runbook published prior to pilot start.
design_considerations_and_tradeoffs:
- Strict region-only residency gives the strongest compliance posture but increases risk of capacity exhaustion; we need soft-fallback semantics for emergencies.
- Enforcing throughput SLAs requires reservation of headroom which increases cost; propose tiered pricing to cover reserved capacity.
- Multi-zone-balanced reduces single-zone blast radius at the cost of slightly higher cross-az network egress; will quantify in cost model.
- Prefer policy-first API that decouples owner intent (residency/SLA) from low-level placement tokens to allow future scheduling improvements.
decisions_made:
1) Default placement policy for new Dedicated fleets will be 'multi-zone-balanced' unless customer chooses 'region-strict'.
2) Cross-region failover is disabled by default and requires a signed opt-in and billing uplift.
3) Throughput SLA will be enforced by a mix of reserved GPU capacity and weight-based request routing; initial SLA unit is 'tokens/sec' per-route.
4) Audit logs and immutable residency labels will be emitted to customer KMS-backed storage for enterprise customers.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (Design & API spec) - finalize policy enum, billing model, and telemetry schema (this ticket).
Phase 1 (Engineering pilot) - implement placement guards, SLA config, and simulator tests; onboard 1 internal customer.
Phase 2 (Customer pilot) - 3 selected customers with contract amendments and runbook drills.
Phase 3 (GA) - console rollout, self-serve opt-in for cross-region failover, publish pricing.
Each phase will have a go/no-go checklist including compliance sign-off.
risk_and_mitigation:
Risk: Customers may unintentionally opt into weaker residency via UI complexity -> Mitigation: add prominent residency confirmation modal and policy comparison matrix.
Risk: SLA enforcement could starve best-effort customers during incidents -> Mitigation: implement graceful degradation and dynamic burst pools that preserve critical SLAs.
Risk: Cross-region failover opt-in may violate contractual residency obligations -> Mitigation: require legal attestation and track in customer metadata.
telemetry_and_metrics:
- Reserved vs used tokens/sec per-tenant
- Failover events by type (zone, node, region)
- Latency P50/P95 for SLA-tagged routes
- Audit log entries with placement decision id
- Economic metric: reserved GPU-hours vs actual utilization
pricing_and_billing_notes: Introduce a 'throughput SLA add-on' priced as a % uplift on committed capacity plus a per-token surcharge for guaranteed headroom. Billing will separate 'reserved capacity fee' and 'SLA premium' line items. Finance needs final rates and billing timeline before pilot.
security_and_compliance:
- Residency labels are immutable and provided in audit logs.
- Customers requiring KMS-backed audit stores will have an integration path that exports placement and failover events.
- Security review required for API that allows cross-region opt-in; plan scheduled with Security on 2025-02-20.
